record.original_question: For a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism on a closed symplectic manifold, is it true that either the number of periodic orbits is finite or the number P(T) of primitive periodic orbits of period at most T grows at least quadratically, in the sense that lim inf_{T -> +infinity} log P(T) / log T >= 2?

Instead, we would like to propose the problem of investigating whether the same phenomenon holds in any dimension. artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,\omega)$ be a closed symplectic manifold and let $\varphi: M \to M$ be a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism, i.e., the time-one map of a (time-dependent) Hamiltonian flow on $M$. A periodic orbit of $\varphi$ of period $k \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1}$ is a finite sequence $(x, \varphi(x), \varphi^2(x), \dots, \varphi^{k-1}(x))$ with $\varphi^k(x) = x$; the orbit is called primitive of period $k$ if $k$ is the smallest such positive integer. For $T > 0$, let
$$P(T) = \#\{\text{primitive periodic orbits of }\varphi\text{ of period at most }T\}.$$
Decide whether the following dichotomy holds for every closed symplectic manifold $(M,\omega)$ and every Hamiltonian diffeomorphism $\varphi$ of $M$: either $\varphi$ has only finitely many periodic orbits (counted over all periods), or
$$\liminf_{T \to +\infty} \frac{\log P(T)}{\log T} \;\geq\; 2.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem extending known surface/two-dimensional results (related to the Conley and Hofer–Zehnder conjectures) to arbitrary dimensions. Web searches turn up active recent work on Hamiltonian periodic orbit growth and pseudo-rotations, but no resolution of the quadratic-growth dichotomy in higher dimensions; the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Conley Conjecture Revisited
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms with more than the minimum number of fixed points and infinite periodic orbits.
status_evidence.claim: Related conjectures on existence of infinitely many periodic orbits remain a guiding theme; quantitative quadratic-growth dichotomy not established in general.

status_evidence.title: On the Hofer-Zehnder conjecture for non-contractible periodic orbits
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on the Hofer–Zehnder conjecture in Hamiltonian dynamics.
status_evidence.claim: Active research on whether finitely many periodic orbits forces pseudo-rotation behavior; growth-rate refinement still being investigated.
